newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline rallies sharply as U.K. budget looms.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline rallies sharply as U.K. budget looms.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices rallied sharply on Friday after crude and gasoline futures sprung higher, but traders were divided over the market's next move ahead of the U.K. budget on Nov 26.

A sharp price drop this week toward Dec swap values may have discounted expectations for a vicious selloff after the budget when U.K. inventories and exports were expected to hit the market again, some traders said.
In addition, light end-user demand appeared to cushion gasoline barges below $210 as the backwardation was punctured and some cargoes headed to the U.S.
"We've all waited for prices to come down and with Dec swaps at $210 it has closed the bridge...and there is a bit more end-user buying," an ARA barge trader said.
But some traders still believed demand was satisfied and prices will fall when the crutches of the budget and the arbitrage were knocked away.
"I think going into December and out of the budget, oil has to flow and exports will come out of the U.K.," a broker said.
The British government has committed itself to raising excise duty of gasoline by five percent annually plus the rate of inflation, so a hike of 3.0-3.2 pence a litre at the pump is expected.
U.S. gasoline traders, meanwhile, said at least 2.3 million barrels of gasoline were expected to arrive in New York Harbor in the last decade of November.
Eurograde last traded at $215.50 fob ARA for a 3,000 tonne barge, up $8 from yesterday, and regular unleaded barges gained $3.50 to $204.50, traders said.
Eurograde cargoes were notionally valued up $5 at $228/$230 cif and regular unleaded up $3 at $217/$219.
Brent crude erased nearly 30 cents of its gains by late in the day but it dit not appear to dent gasoline's rally.
